state.title: Make agent-user.test.ts pass under any umask
state.task:
Owner asked for this on 2026-10-14. Keep it small enough to finish within an hour, and end with a pull request. The task is not done until the PR is open.

Problem: `api/tests/security/agent-user.test.ts` (in the `security` sub-suite) passes only under umask 022. Under umask 077, which Jevellan thread shells use and some runners may use too, 2 cases fail. A run on 2026-10-14 confirmed it: the suite went red under 077, and the same file passed 23/23 under a process-local umask 022 on Node 20.

Likely cause (verify it): the fixtures create files and folders with an explicit `mode` (for example `writeFileSync(..., { mode: 0o644 })` at lines ~323-328 and ~402-409, `mkdirSync(..., { mode: 0o755 })`). The umask masks those modes (0o644 becomes 0o600 under 077). Assertions that expect untouched entries to keep their fixture mode then fail, for example `expect(mode(outside)).toBe(0o755)` and `expect(mode(join(outside, 'secret.txt'))).toBe(0o644)`, and the fixture modes the code under test reads differ too. Some fixtures already follow `writeFileSync`/`mkdirSync` with `chmodSync`, but not all.

Fix:
- Make every fixture set its mode explicitly with `chmodSync` after creating the entry, so the setup is the same under any umask. Do not assert on umask-derived modes.
- If any failing assertion is about a mode the product code (the agent-user module the test covers, under `api/src/`) itself creates and relies on the ambient umask for, that is a security-relevant product bug. Set the mode explicitly in the product code, not in the test, and say so in the PR.
- Do not change the umask globally for the test run, and do not loosen the assertions on what the product code sets.

Verify:
- Run the file under both umasks, e.g. `(umask 022 && npx vitest run api/tests/security/agent-user.test.ts)` and `(umask 077 && npx vitest run api/tests/security/agent-user.test.ts)`, or through the repo's vitest config. Use Node 20.
- Then run `npm run test:suite -- security --unit`.
- Never run `mobile`, `expensive` or `npm run test:all`.

Docs: add a short "Recently fixed" entry to `docs/findings.md` (slug `agent-user-test-umask`): the cause, the fix, and proof under both umasks.

Report: the cause, whether product code changed, the two umask runs' results, the security sub-suite totals, and the PR link.

Goal: Hardening through automated tests. Why it matters: Nothing in Ekoa should break without a test noticing. Every finding ends in a test or a written dismissal, and the nightly suite stays green.

Task type: fix.

Rules for every thread:
Ekoa Code rules:
- Follow the repository's own agent instructions.
- Never edit evals/ or anything that defines how the legal programme is measured.
- Never touch production (go.ekoa.io) or deploy; never run token-spending tests.
- Test accounts only in the office named "(APAGAR)". Ekoa never sends WhatsApp messages.
- Secrets live only in GitHub secrets; never add one to the repository.
- Check user-facing changes at 390 px width as well as desktop.
- When you add to docs/decisions.md or docs/findings.md, add new entries at the end only.
